findings.location: The steam snapshot resolver / The store pull — "a `name` over `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS` or carrying control bytes (the `013-B4` bound `027-C3` names — the pull never writes one, §The store pull)"
findings.problem: new: the parenthetical is asserted in the changed text but no pull rule backs it. §The store pull's named refusals are non-`200`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `3xx`, over-`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS`, wrong envelope, page-budget, non-decimal `appid`, and "The one *dropped*, not refused, case is a record whose `name` breaks the `013-B4` bound" — per A10 that bound is `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS = 128` alone; the control-byte rule is the loader's separate refusal. A pulled record whose name carries an ASCII control byte is therefore neither refused nor dropped: it is published, the next load refuses the file, and "a present-but-unloadable snapshot that the pull then cannot replace is a named startup refusal" does not save the operator because the pull can replace it and re-publishes the same unloadable bytes — the run serves from memory while every later restart is a named refusal unless `--no-steam`. Same remote-content-into-availability-cliff class this pass set out to clear, one rule from the drop rule that now exists.
findings.fix: Widen the one dropped case to "a record whose `name` breaks the `013-B4` octet bound **or carries a control byte**" (the two refusals the loader already names), so the parenthetical becomes the rule it points at.

findings.location: Issued entries, mint rule step 5 — "mints `steam-<appid>`, spelled from the queried key's external id … appid-unique"
findings.problem: new: spelling the fallback from the client's digits makes the id depend on the queried spelling of one appid. `steam/42` and `steam/0042` are both admissible (`keys.rs:73` bounds length, token set and path safety only — I verified there is no appid bound), and the design never pins how the "one exact-`appid` probe" treats them. Numeric match: one snapshot record mints `steam-42` and `steam-0042`, two held ids for one game, so "appid-unique" is false and step 4's suffix has no stated appid source (`mint.rs::mint_id(display_name, appid, held)` carries one `appid` for both jobs). Textual match: `steam/0042` is not present in the snapshot, takes the second bullet, and answers a false `200 []` for an appid the catalog holds — the claim `027-L3` exists to police.
findings.fix: Name the canonical spelling in step 5 and at the probe: spell the fallback from the snapshot record's `appid` (or refuse a non-canonical decimal external id before the probe, saying which); keep `MAX_DISCOVERY_SLUG_OCTETS` as the cited arithmetic, which is verified correct.

findings.location: Budgets — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — 50k *worst-legal* records at ~240 octets"
findings.problem: re-raised (r1 nit, narrowed but not closed): ~240 octets costs the name at its 128-octet *decoded* bound, but the response body carries JSON string escapes, so a quote- or backslash-heavy name serializes at up to 2× and a record lands near 340 octets — a legal 50k page of such names is ~17 MiB, over the cap, and the design must refuse that page and fail the pull (a startup refusal) on a legal response.
findings.fix: One clause saying which the cap is chosen for: either double the name allowance for escapes in the derivation (⌈2 × 128⌉) or pin `max_results` from the worst-escaped record.

findings.location: Hosted mode / Risks / Deferred — "`dropped_appids` is not a health fact — the pull writing the list prints it" beside "its `appid` is listed in the snapshot's `dropped_appids`, which is the operator's signal to pursue that amendment"
findings.problem: new: with the fact off `health` (rightly, per `027-C3`) and off `stats` (Deferred), the operator's only channels are one stdout line at publish time and opening the snapshot file; Rollout 6 enumerates "reading the retired list's size against its cap" but never the dropped list, so the signal the design leans on twice has no runbook line and no restart-surviving surface.
findings.fix: Add the dropped list to Rollout 6's reading duty in the same clause as the retired-list size; no new surface needed.

findings.location: The store pull — "sized in §Budgets to cover this grid with its retries, so a slow store costs a late snapshot, not a guaranteed failure"
findings.problem: new: true for the background delta, not for the pre-bind full pull, where the same 1,872 s grid ends in `027-C3`'s named startup refusal after ~31 minutes of a process that has not bound. This pass deleted the sentence that bounded that path ("the pre-bind full pull is paced by the socket timeouts and a seconds-scale retry, never an hour-long sleep") while raising `STEAM_PULL_DEADLINE_SECONDS` from 900 to 1,920, so nothing states what a slow store costs an operator's start.
findings.fix: Scope the clause — "costs a late delta; a full pull that runs the grid is the named `steam pull deadline` startup refusal" — and keep the deadline value, which is arithmetically right.

findings.location: §The store pull — "a list that would exceed `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS` is itself a named pull failure" (with §Budgets' `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS = 1_024`, §The steam snapshot resolver's "the list merges as a set on delta … and resets only on a full-pull replace", §Risks' "a 43-character CJK or 32-character emoji title reaches it", §Rollout 6's "forcing a full refresh by deleting the snapshot")
findings.problem: New mechanism introduced by this revision. The cap's breach re-imports, by accumulation, the posture the drop exists to avoid ("failing the pull over one is remote, permanent denial of the supply"). The list only grows on delta — an entry clears only when a delta re-delivers that appid with a within-bound `name`, and "Deltas never see removals"; a failed pull publishes nothing, so `fetched_at` never advances, so the next delta asks the same `if_modified_since` window and re-sees the same over-bound record, making the breach permanent rather than transient. The consequence is the r1 blast radius reached by count: the snapshot ages past `STEAM_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`, the policy's last bullet turns every steam miss into a named `503`, and per §Compatibility matrix a bound CLI "fail[s] the whole scan closed". Recovery is refused by the same rule: entries leave the list only via a delta showing them within bound, so a list at 1,024 is a subset of the catalog's currently over-bound records and implies a full pull that also breaches — the runbook's recovery lever is refused too, leaving `--no-steam` (the terminal state). The loader carries the same cap ("a `dropped_appids` longer than `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS`"), so a drifted file plus a refusing pull is a startup refusal. Signals are thin: r2 removed the count from health ("`dropped_appids` is not a health fact — the pull writing the list prints it"), `stats` is `{games, source_keys, revision, issued}`, and Rollout 6 watches only "the retired list's size against its cap". Likelihood is low (A10 sets 128 as "one octet above the longest surveyed store title"), so this is priced rather than gated.
findings.fix: Make the breach degrade instead of denying: replace "a list that would exceed `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS` is itself a named pull failure" with publishing the capped list under the whole-list posture (the r1 posture retained only here, where the unenumerated set genuinely is unknown), so a breach costs miss certification, not the supply or the recovery path. If fail-the-pull stands, price it in the §Risks row and §Budgets with scope (all steam misses via the age bound), trigger (≥1,025 over-bound names in one inter-full-pull interval, cumulative on deltas), permanence (a failed delta never advances `fetched_at`) and recovery, and add the list's length to Rollout 6's watch line beside the retired file's size.

findings.location: §Budgets — "on top of it a mint holds one model plus one serialized buffer, and a delta merge the old snapshot, the merged model, one serialize buffer and the current page body"
findings.problem: The sentence rewritten to answer my r1 transient finding still enumerates an incomplete family: it omits the full pull, the process's largest transient, whose input cap this same revision raised (`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS` 8,388,608 → 12,582,912, justified because "the pinned `max_results` can answer that page, not the ~150-octet mid-estimate" — that arithmetic is sound: 50k worst-legal records at ~217–230 octets ≈ 11.4 MiB). But 12 pages × 12.58 MiB is a 151 MiB admissible input envelope against one gate on the other side, `027-B1`'s 33,554,432 publish-time check: the pull may legitimately read ~4.7× more record bytes than the document may hold, and pays the whole read before refusing. A full pull accumulates every page before publishing (it "replaces the snapshot"), so its peak is the model over up to 600k `{appid, name}` records plus the appid index plus the current page body, on top of the corpus/issued/retired documents boot already loaded (16+64+32 MiB at caps). "144 MiB of JSON … as the boot load ceiling" is a load bound being read as the process's memory story.
findings.fix: One clause in the same sentence naming the full pull's transient and its bound — check the `027-B1` publish ceiling as pages accumulate, or state that ≤12 pages of records is the process's largest transient — so all three writer transients (mint, delta merge, full pull) are on the table that §Deferred's batched-writes deferral defers against.

findings.location: §The store pull — "sized in §Budgets to cover this grid with its retries, so a slow store costs a late snapshot, not a guaranteed failure"; §Budgets — "`STEAM_PULL_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 1_920` ≥ the grid that family authorizes (`12 × (3 × 32 + 2 × 30) = 1,872)`"
findings.problem: The relation and the named `steam pull deadline` refusal close my r1 finding (12 × 156 = 1,872 ≤ 1,920 checks out), but the grid charges each attempt `STEAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT + STEAM_READ_TIMEOUT` = 32 s as though those bounded a page, while the framing the design says it copies hand-rolls them as socket timeouts (`apps/registry/src/upstream.rs:97` `set_read_timeout(Some(constants::UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT))`, body read to completion), which bound one `read` call — a steadily trickling body never trips the 30 s bound, so a page's legal wall time is unbounded and the grid is a floor, not a ceiling. Its real precondition is ~393 KiB/s per worst-legal page (12,582,912/32 s), leaving the deadline as the only wall-clock bound; a typical catalog (≈11–16 MiB) finishes with room, so it bites only worst-legal pages on a slow link, where the honest outcome is the refusal. Second half: on the pre-bind path a deadline-killed pull is a startup refusal, so the unstated figure is that `serve`, and `query` with its "same startup as `serve` including load-or-pull", can block up to 1,920 s before binding.
findings.fix: One clause stating whether the two timeouts bound a read or a page (and, if a read, that the grid is a floor and the deadline is the only page-total bound), plus one naming the worst-case pre-bind block as ≤1,920 s before bind, so the runbook's start-timeout and restart-policy line has a number to sit against.

findings.location: §The steam snapshot resolver — "`dropped_appids` is the ascending, duplicate-free list of the `appid`s the pull dropped for the `013-B4` name bound; normally empty" (+ §The hosted lookup policy step 5 — "The key's appid is listed in `dropped_appids`: the named `503` `steam snapshot incomplete`")
findings.problem: new. The r2 answer to the over-bound-name problem adds a bookkeeping subsystem where the repo already ships the rule for this data class, and its answer to "one store title is too long" is to make that game permanently unanswerable. r2 adds: a field in a contract document the ADR fixes (027-C3's shape {version, fetched_at, apps}), costing a Rollout-1 `amended-by` on the ADR this run implements; a new constant; set-merge/self-clear/reset semantics across deltas; four new loader refusals plus two Test-strategy rows; and a new policy branch whose served consequence, per §Compatibility matrix ("a bound CLI fails the whole scan closed"), is that a user owning a long-named title can never complete `discovery list` — the appid is not in `apps`, so the mint path cannot fire and the answer is `503` forever, against 027-S1's "every other steam key answers from the snapshot on day one".
findings.fix: Use the shipped rule: `crates/discovery/src/game.rs::friendly_name` already clamps a store display name to "the longest `char`-boundary prefix inside `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS`" ("a truncated display string costs a shorter label, never a different identity"), and `apps/registry` already depends on `discovery` (Cargo.toml:14), so it is an import, not a dependency. Normalize an over-bound (or control-byte) name at the pull seam into the 013-B4-legal form instead of dropping it: the appid stays in the snapshot, no miss needs un-certifying, 027-C3 ships verbatim with no amendment, and the mint's existing steps absorb the rest (the fold never exceeds the name's octets; two titles sharing a 128-octet prefix collide at step 4 and fall to step 5's `steam-<appid>`; 027-L2 plus policy step 2 mean derivation is paid once per key). Replaces by name: the drop rule and `dropped_appids` in §The store pull, §The steam snapshot resolver, policy step 5's third bullet, §Risks row 7, §Deferred's fourth bullet, Rollout 1's 027-C3 line, Rollout 3, Test #2/#3/#6/#13, `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS`, and the pull's "prints it" line — one normalization sentence in their place. Counter stated honestly: `friendly_name`'s comment rests on "nothing parses the result", false here since the mint derives from this name; 027-L2 + policy step 2 + steps 4–5 are what make the clamp admissible in the registry.

findings.location: §Budgets — "`MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS = 1_024` (its breach is the named pull failure, §The store pull)" (+ §The store pull — "a list that would exceed `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS` is itself a named pull failure", "the list merges as a set on delta … and resets only on a full-pull replace")
findings.problem: new. The cap's number and its breach consequence together cancel the property the mechanism was added for — the same mid-estimate error this revision just corrected one line earlier for `MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS`. One page the design calls legal carries 50,000 dropped records: a 50,000-record page of 129-octet names is ~207 octets/record ≈ 10.4 MB, inside `MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` and inside `max_results=50000` — so a single page exceeds the cap ~49×, and a full pull's worst legal drop count is 12 × 50k = 600k, ~590×. In steady state the list only grows: the refresh thread delta-pulls and never full-pulls, and a restart with a fresh loadable snapshot loads rather than pulls, so a reset needs the operator to delete the file. On breach the design returns to the r0 posture the Revision log rejected — a named pull failure, i.e. a stale snapshot aging into `503` for every steam miss, and a startup refusal to bind — reached by remote-chosen content, which the same section says the mechanism exists to prevent. §Risks row 7's "impact Low" holds only on the unstated premise that the cap is never breached.
findings.fix: Adopt the clamp above and the constant disappears; if the list stays, make saturation a posture and not a pull failure — while `dropped_appids` is full, no appid miss is certifiable (exactly the r1 `incomplete` posture, as the overflow case) — and size the cap from the page budget rather than a guess. Either change replaces the named pull failure and adds no mechanism.

findings.location: §Budgets — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — 50k *worst-legal* records at ~240 octets (A17's four fields, `name` at `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS`), because the pinned `max_results` can answer that page, not the ~150-octet mid-estimate"
findings.problem: new. The re-sizing is right for the mid-estimate reason and wrong for the "worst-legal" claim: its premise (`name` at 128 octets) is exactly what §The store pull's drop case denies — names over the bound are the content the design expects to arrive, so no finite page cap is worst-legal and a page heavy with over-bound names is legal content that trips a named page refusal and fails the pull. The constant is a read budget wearing a worst-case label, and the label is what a reader trusts when the budgets are re-derived.
findings.fix: One clause: name it the response read budget it is, record that over-bound names make the true worst case unbounded so an over-cap page is the residual §Risks carries (the same posture as the previous finding's fix), and drop the word "worst-legal". A relabel plus one risk clause, no new mechanism.

findings.location: §Issued entries — "safe because the append is a set insert, so an already-present id is a no-op" beside "A delete whose append would breach the cap is the named refusal `retired id list full` and mutates nothing"
findings.problem: new. Read literally, "would breach" tests the candidate entry, so a no-op append against an at-cap list refuses the very retry the same paragraph promises completes the removal.
findings.fix: Three words: the cap is checked against "the buffer the write renames" — the check the paragraph already names for the other documents.

reply.summary: Finding 1 (major): the `dropped_appids` subsystem is deleted end-to-end — the snapshot ships `027-C3`'s shape verbatim, the store pull instead normalizes an over-bound or control-byte `name` at the pull seam with the shipped `discovery::friendly_name` clamp (A7 now carries its basis and caveat) and keeps the record, so no appid miss needs un-certifying; removed the policy step-5 `steam snapshot incomplete` branch, its loader refusals, the health/pull-print line, the delta merge/clear/reset rules, Rollout 1's `amended-by` on `027-C3`, Rollout 3's fact, and Test #2/#3/#6/#13 rows, replaced by one normalization passage plus one Risks row. Finding 2 (major): `MAX_DROPPED_APPIDS`, its cap breach as a named pull failure, and its monotonic-growth posture disappear with the constant. Finding 3 (minor): `MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS` is relabeled the response read budget ("worst-legal" dropped) with the unbounded-true-worst-case over-cap page recorded as the §Risks residual. Finding 4 (nit): the retired-id cap is measured against the buffer the write renames, so a no-op re-delete against an at-cap list still completes; Test #5 pins it. The three FYI points fall out (no ADR self-amendment, clamp count on the publish line replaces the 1,024-appid log line). Revision log amended in place at the three affected entries. Net −15 lines.
reply.commitMessage: docs: normalize over-bound store names at the pull seam instead of tracking dropped appids

findings.location: §The store pull — "The rule is the shipped `discovery::friendly_name` one, through the existing `discovery` dependency (A7) — whitespace collapse then the longest `char`-boundary prefix inside `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS`, with control bytes dropped in the same pass" (also A7's new clause, §Options "an over-bound name is normalized, not dropped", §The hosted lookup policy step 5 "every record the pull was handed is in it", §The steam snapshot resolver's loader refusal, §Test strategy #6, Rollout 3)
findings.problem: new. The clause is false against the code A7 marks `verified`: `crates/discovery/src/game.rs:102-113` is `split_whitespace().join(" ")` then an `is_char_boundary` clamp — those two operations only. `char::is_whitespace` covers `\t \n \u{b} \u{c} \r` and U+001C–U+001F/U+0085, so NUL, `\u{1}`–`\u{8}`, `\u{e}`–`\u{1b}` (ESC), DEL and C1 survive into the snapshot name. The design's own loader refuses exactly that content — "a `name` over `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS` or carrying control bytes (… the pull normalizes one before writing it)" — so with the shipped rule as cited, the instance publishes a document its own loader will not read: every restart takes the "else pull in full" branch, and a restart during a store/key outage (the §Risks A6 row) is a named startup refusal instead of serving the last snapshot — the remote-chosen denial of supply r3 exists to delete, back through the loader. §Test strategy #6 ("a bound-breaking or control-byte `name` is clamped to the `013-B4`-legal form") also pins behavior `friendly_name` does not have, so the suite fails or the implementer adds the strip step the document says is already shipped. The r3 deletion's premise covers the name-bound half and not the control-byte half; A7's own description of the shipped rule ("whitespace collapse plus the longest `char`-boundary prefix") is accurate and contradicts the body clause.
findings.fix: Delete "with control bytes dropped in the same pass" and name the one line the registry owns instead: the pull seam drops `char::is_control()` characters before the `friendly_name` clamp (a std filter — no constant, no document, no policy branch, no ADR amendment), mirrored in A7 and Rollout 3's "`friendly_name` name normalization". Keep the loader's control-byte refusal as the contract-document discipline it is. One clause plus one named filter replaces the false reuse; nothing else r3 removed needs restoring.

findings.location: §Budgets — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — the response *read* budget for one page, 50k records at ~240 octets"
findings.problem: new. The relabel resolves my r1 "worst-legal" finding, but the derivation still reads as a product that does not produce the constant: 50,000 × ~240 = 12,000,000, while 12,582,912 is 12 MiB (≈252 octets per record). A reader re-deriving the budget gets a different number than the shipped one.
findings.fix: Word it as the sum it is: "— 12 MiB, which the 50k-records-at-~240-octets estimate sits inside —".

findings.location: §The store pull (and §Test strategy #6) — "whitespace collapse then the longest `char`-boundary prefix inside `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS`"
findings.problem: new. No disposition for a name that normalizes to empty: a whitespace-only title (and, once the control strip is owned, an all-control title) clamps to `""`, which r2's pass-through could not produce. The identity is safe — mint step 3 mints `steam-<appid>` — but the issued record and the served candidate carry `name: ""`, where the shipped ingest rule treats empty as a fault ("`name` is outside the 1-128-octet bound", apps/registry/src/upstream.rs:247) while the record gate the issued document reuses checks only the upper bound (apps/registry/src/corpus.rs:424), so nothing refuses it.
findings.fix: One clause: "a name that normalizes to empty is stored empty — its label renders blank and its identity is step 3's `steam-<appid>`" — or substitute a single space. No mechanism either way.

findings.location: A7 / §The store pull / Rollout 3 — "`discovery::friendly_name`"
findings.problem: new. Not the shipped path: `crates/discovery/src/lib.rs` publishes `pub mod game;` with no crate-root re-export, and every shipped caller writes `use discovery::game::{… friendly_name}`. The design the code review pins misnames the import.
findings.fix: Spell it `discovery::game::friendly_name` in A7's basis and Rollout 3.

reply.summary: Major (control-byte strip miscredited to the shipped clamp): deleted the false clause 'with control bytes dropped in the same pass' and the restatement of the rule in §Risks; §The store pull now states the one line the registry owns — drop `char::is_control()` characters, then the shipped `friendly_name` clamp — with A7 rewritten to the verified shipped rule (whitespace collapse + char-boundary clamp only, `split_whitespace` leaves NUL/ESC/DEL/C1 in place, basis now also `crates/discovery/src/lib.rs`), mirrored in Test strategy #6 and Rollout 3, and the loader's control-byte refusal left as the contract-document discipline; also deleted §The steam snapshot resolver's duplicate 'every appid the pull was handed is in it' claim, consolidated into §The hosted lookup policy step 5. Nit (Budgets arithmetic): `MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS` now reads as 12 MiB, above the 50k-at-~240-octets estimate, so the constant stops looking derived. Nit (empty-normalized name): one clause — it stores empty, renders blank, identity is mint step 3's `steam-<appid>` — plus its Test #6 pin. Nit (path): `discovery::game::friendly_name` spelled correctly in A7, §The store pull and Rollout 3. Revision log maintained in place: the over-bound-names entry is superseded in place (r0→r4) and the page-budget entry amended, not appended. Net +1 line (three deletions/consolidations against the two dispositions that needed new wording).

findings.location: §The store pull — "The publish line counts the names it clamped (§Risks, §Deferred)"
findings.problem: new (from the revised text). The revision made the registry own a second normalization — the `char::is_control()` strip — but the only count anywhere is still the clamp count, and §Risks ("the pull's clamp count is the signal") and §Deferred ("the pull's clamp count is the operator's signal") both name that count as the sole operator signal feeding the deferred `013-B4`/`027-C3` bound re-sizing decision. A store answering with control-byte-laden titles is therefore normalized invisibly, and a name that becomes in-budget because it was stripped never reaches the count that decides whether the bound needs re-sizing.
findings.fix: One word: "The publish line counts the names it normalized (clamped or control-stripped)" — or, if the split is deliberate, one clause here saying control-strip events are deliberately not counted as bound pressure. No new counter, constant, or log line either way.

findings.location: §Options "Partial snapshot serving" — "of the games-only set (§The store pull normalizes, never drops)"; §Risks `013-B4` row — "keeps the record (§The store pull owns the rule)"
findings.problem: new (introduced by this revision). Two parentheticals where the `§` sigil binds to a clause instead of a heading: no section is named "The store pull normalizes, never drops" or "The store pull owns the rule", so the cross-reference resolves only by guesswork, unlike every other `§`-ref in the document.
findings.fix: Put the assertion outside the sigil: "(§The store pull: it normalizes, never drops)" and "(the rule is §The store pull's)". No text deleted.

findings.location: §The store pull / §Risks / §Deferred — "The publish line counts the names it clamped (§Risks, §Deferred)" beside "the pull's clamp count is the operator's signal"
findings.problem: re-raised (same class as round 1's dropped-list signal nit, which the revision answered by substituting a new signal for the deleted one). The signal named in three sections has no surface the design defines and no runbook duty: "the publish line" appears nowhere else in the document — §The store pull names only the startup `registry hosted listening` line and the refresh thread's failure warning line — the count is not in `health` (correctly excluded, since `027-C3` fixes that fact to `{games, fetched_at}`) nor in `stats` (counts only, and its own item is Deferred), and Rollout 6's reading duty enumerates "reading the retired list's size against its cap" but never the clamp count. So the §Deferred amendment trigger ("if a store name breaches it in earnest") is observable only on the stdout of the run that pulled, does not survive a restart, and no runbook line tells the operator to read it.
findings.fix: One clause in Rollout 6's reading list — the clamp count on the pull's publish line, naming where it is printed — beside the retired-list size it already carries; no new surface needed.

findings.location: §Budgets / §Risks — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — the response *read* budget for one page … not a worst case, since over-bound store names make a page's true size unbounded and the over-cap page is the residual §Risks carries"
findings.problem: re-raised (round 1's arithmetic nit, narrowed but not closed by the relabel). The residual is attributed to one cause only. Over-bound names are not the only way a *legal* page breaches 12 MiB: the body carries JSON string escapes, so a name at its 128-octet decoded bound serializes at up to 2x when quote- or backslash-heavy (~340 octets per record, ~17 MiB for the pinned 50k page) and more for characters the encoder emits as `\u00XX`. §Risks also states the cost as only "a page refusal that keeps the previous snapshot until `027-B2`'s age bound" — the steady-state half; on a cold instance with no snapshot the same named page refusal is the named startup refusal, and the operator's only way to bind is `--no-steam`, i.e. every Steam key answering `503` and every bound CLI scan failing closed (§Compatibility matrix). The cap's arithmetic itself checks out: 12,582,912 > 50,000 x ~240.
findings.fix: Extend the clause §Deferred's item already asks for: name JSON-escaped serialization, not only over-bound names, as the second way a legal page breaches the read budget, and say the cold-start branch is the named startup refusal; keep the constant's value unchanged.

findings.location: §The store pull / Test strategy #6 — "A name that normalizes to empty stays empty: its label renders blank and its identity is mint step 3's `steam-<appid>`" and "an all-whitespace or all-control title stores empty"
findings.problem: new (introduced by this revision; round 1 dropped such a record instead). The blank is not confined to the registry: that `name` is what the mint persists into the issued record and what the candidate contract serves, and `apps/discovery-cli/src/catalog.rs:46-47` documents the candidate `name` as "the name the prompt shows", accepting any string there (`catalog.rs:393-401`). A store title consisting only of control or whitespace characters therefore reaches a user's confirmation prompt as an invisible option, chosen by remote content — the one piece of attacker-chosen content this pass lets through to a user's decision point. (No validation cliff: `corpus.rs:424` bounds `name` only above, so the issued document still loads, and identity is unique via mint step 3.)
findings.fix: One clause giving the empty case a label the registry owns instead of nothing: store `steam-<appid>` (already mint step 3's spelling, no new constant) as the `name` when normalization yields empty, and let #6 assert that in place of "stores empty".

findings.location: [new] §The store pull — "`discovery::game::friendly_name` through that existing `discovery` dependency (A7: the shipped rule is whitespace and clamping only, which is why the filter is ours)"
findings.problem: The revision makes a shipped display-convention function load-bearing for identity, against its own stated contract. `025-C2` says the friendly name "is never end-user visible ..., participates in no join, and carries no derivation law", and the function's doc-comment says the clamp is admissible "here and only here" because "nothing parses the result, it is never joined to anything, and it is never user-visible" (crates/discovery/src/game.rs:96-100). This design inverts all three: the output is persisted into a contract document, served to bound CLIs as the candidate `name`, and fed to mint steps 1-5, whose output is immortal under `027-L2`. Because `025-C2` deliberately gives `friendly_name` no derivation law, nothing pins it: a display-side change in `crates/discovery` (whitespace set, clamp rule) silently changes every identity minted afterwards, with no gate and no ledger annotation.
findings.fix: Have `apps/registry` own the two-line rule (a `char::is_control()` strip, whitespace collapse, longest `char`-boundary prefix) as its own named function pinned by Test strategy #6, replacing the cross-crate call with the copy it pins. If the call is kept instead, the smallest fix is a registry suite asserting the two rules byte-exactly plus a Rollout-1 line making a `friendly_name` change a mint-stability event.

findings.location: [re-raised] §Issued entries, mint steps 4/6 × §Test strategy #1 — step 6: "Any spelling the rule lands on that is held or retired by a different record refuses the mint with the named `503` `mint identity held`" vs #1: "a suffixed id already held takes `steam-<appid>`, a held `steam-<appid>` refuses `mint identity held`"
findings.problem: The contradiction I filed in r1 is still open and the revision widened it: r1's fixture said "already held by a curated record", the new text says "already held", so the unstated plain → suffixed → `steam-<appid>` cascade now covers every holder. Step 5's fallback triggers on length only, never on held-ness, so the rule text refuses exactly what the suite pins as a fallback, and implementations match suites.
findings.fix: State the cascade in step 4's own sentence ("a suffixed id that is itself held or retired takes `steam-<appid>`; if that is held or retired, step 6 refuses") and reduce step 6's "any spelling" breadth to the three named spellings.

findings.location: [re-raised] §Test strategy #1 — "including the over-bound cases the arithmetic allows: a 128-octet ASCII name, a 128-octet digit-leading name, and a 128-octet *colliding* name all mint `steam-<appid>`"
findings.problem: Still contradicts §Issued entries step 5, which this revision restated ("The fold never exceeds the name's octets, but steps 2 and 4 add them"): a 128-octet ASCII name with no leading digit and no collision folds to at most exactly 128 octets, and `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS` is endpoint-inclusive (crates/core/src/placement.rs:83), so it mints its own slug. The new sentence compounds it in the other direction: "an id still over `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS` after substitution refuses `mint identity over bound`" is unreachable through any admissible key, since keys.rs caps the whole joined key at 128 and `steam-` costs 6. The suite thus pins a legal at-bound slug as a fallback and pins a production-impossible refusal.
findings.fix: Drop "a 128-octet ASCII name" from that fixture list (the digit-leading and colliding names are the over-bound cases) and mark the `mint identity over bound` case a unit-only defensive branch, or delete it.

findings.location: [new] §Options — "Nothing else a legal pull is handed makes the snapshot short of the games-only set (§The store pull normalizes, never drops)" and §Risks — "The pull seam normalizes the `name` to the `013-B4`-legal form and keeps the record (§The store pull owns the rule)"
findings.problem: Both revisions cross-reference section titles that do not exist; the section is "The store pull (traces `027-C3`, `027-B4`, `027-L1`, `027-L4`)". The document's tracing discipline reads those anchors as pointers.
findings.fix: Point both at §The store pull, as §Deferred already does.

findings.location: [new] §Budgets — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — ... above the 50k-records-at-~240-octets estimate ... the pinned `max_results` can return"
findings.problem: The revision introduces a legitimate-input estimate of ~240 octets per record to size the page budget, while leaving the snapshot's `027-B1` ceiling (33,554,432) unstated against it: at 200k records that ceiling admits an average record of only ~167 octets, so a catalog at the per-record figure this section justifies would breach the publish-time check — which, after this revision, has no fallback posture at all since the `incomplete` machinery is deleted. Real catalogs sit far inside it; the finding is the missing arithmetic, not a predicted outage.
findings.fix: Add the per-record average the 32 MiB ceiling admits at 200k records beside the page estimate, and name a publish-time breach's posture in one clause (the same `027-B1` refusal the loader applies), so both budgets come off one table.

findings.location: [new] §Risks — "the cost is a shorter label, never a different identity"
findings.problem: A clamp can change the identity, not only the label: a title whose first 128 octets are all non-`[a-z0-9]` (an emoji or CJK run) with its Latin title past the bound folds empty and takes step 3's `steam-<appid>` where the unclamped name would have minted the slug. Harmless (the id stays unique and stable), but this is the mitigation row's own claim.
findings.fix: Qualify it: "a shorter label, and a different identity only where the surviving prefix folds empty, which is step 3's fallback".

findings.location: [re-raised] §Assumption register A16 — "legitimate there only because `cargo check` generates no code"
findings.problem: Unchanged from r1 and still in tension with §Options' own correction ("`ring` compiles C and assembly for the *target* through a build script"), which is precisely why Rollout 3 drops `apps/registry` from that leg.
findings.fix: Reword the parenthetical: the cross-check is legitimate today because no other dependency runs a target-native build script.

reply.commitMessage: docs: final language pass on the 027 hosted-registry proposal
test: pin the ADR-027 hosted registry suites
feat: grow the registry library target and the steam store resolver
fix: close the ADR-027 hosted registry gate findings in the binary

test: re-pin the registry suites to ADR-027's hosted mode

Harness (tests/common/mod.rs): Registry::start now supplies the two ADR-027
startup defaults a leg that is not itself about them needs — a sandboxed
temp XDG_DATA_HOME, kept alive for the child's lifetime in the new
Registry::_default_data so Drop kills the process before the tree goes
(027-C4 made a resolvable <data> a startup requirement), and an appended
--no-steam unless the leg spells that flag or the steam key (027-C3 makes a
key-less run a refusal too). expect_refused_startup/run_registry keep the
scrubbed environment with no default, so the startup-refusal suites are
untouched. The steam key variable is now one STEAM_KEY_VAR const shared by
the scrub list and the default's check.

Re-pins, only where the design or an accepted finding changed:
- admin_auth, admin_mutations: stats is exactly {games, issued, revision,
  source_keys} (027-C6, Test strategy #9), and the admin face's document is
  the corpus at its own --corpus path with nothing copied into <data>
  (§The curation face); a delete leg asks a local/… key so its empty answer
  is the join's verdict, not a resolver one.
- candidates_join, response_shape, slug_decoding, persist_and_concurrency:
  empty-answer legs ask local/… keys (never resolver candidates, so 200 []
  rather than the named 503) and the tearing-reader racer races on local/…
  keys so resolver verdicts cannot widen its legal states.
- catalog_document: the two legs that hand a run a document to refuse now
  give it a separate sandboxed <data> plus --no-steam, and the
  document-name leg spells steam-snapshot.json, issued-v1.json,
  retired-ids-v1.json and write.lock.
- data_layout: data_of(envs) resolves <data> per the A2 rule (XDG → APPDATA
  → HOME/.local/share, relative = unset) and each branch's snapshot is
  planted under the <data> it resolves to; the listing leg takes its listing
  after a self-exiting registry query one-shot, since a killed run
  legitimately leaves write.lock.
- hosted_end_to_end: both query one-shots that had nothing to load now plant
  a snapshot, so their exits are the posture under test rather than a store
  pull (and Test strategy #17's no-dial rule holds; the leg that took 61 s
  now takes 0.05 s).
- issued_entries: the contract-refusal fixture is a source_key repeated
  within one record — the refusal 026-C3 actually carries — rather than one
  key in two records, which is a legal two-candidate answer.

Retirement (A15): cache_document, caching_policy, upstream_client and
upstream_endpoint_gate, plus three legs in candidates_join/admin_mutations,
have every leg #[ignore]d with its reason and a header naming where each
surviving half is now pinned (issued_entries, steam, response_shape,
hosted_lookup_policy, hosted_health_stats, hosted_startup). Their subject —
the caching mode, cache-v1.json, --upstream and the upstream health facts —
is retired, not repaired. They are retired in place rather than deleted
because MovePairSchema is a {from,to} rename pair and cannot express a
deletion, and file deletion belongs to the runner: please delete those four
suite files (and, if the build notes call for it, Registry::caching,
FakeUpstream, cache_doc and unreachable_upstream in tests/common/mod.rs).

Gate: cargo test --workspace --locked is green with 0 failures and 29
intentional ignores; cargo fmt --all -- --check and
cargo clippy -p bindforge-registry --all-targets -- -D warnings are clean.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/main.rs:368-401
findings.problem: `load_or_pull_snapshot` accepts any loadable snapshot and pulls only when nothing loadable exists, reversing `027-C3`'s verbatim clause that the snapshot is loaded "if present and within `027-B2`'s freshness, else pulled in full before the process binds" (ADR-027 lines 105-108; proposal 268-273). An instance booted over a snapshot past `STEAM_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` answers `503 steam snapshot stale` for every steam key until the refresh thread's first delta, up to 86,400 s later (main.rs:458-463 counts the startup as the last pull), and a bound CLI fails a whole scan closed on those 503s. No startup leg tests the designed direction (hosted_startup.rs has none; tests/steam.rs:210 only pins that a stale file loads). The comment at main.rs:357-367 claims a §Deviations entry in 03-build-notes.md, which is outside my permitted inputs, so the declaration could not be verified.
findings.fix: Load only a present-and-fresh snapshot; treat past-age (and present-but-unloadable) as the pull case, keeping the named startup refusal for a failed pull; add the `027-C3`/Test-strategy-#8 startup leg. If the posture is intended instead, amend `027-C3` before shipping the code.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/steam.rs:527-545
findings.problem: A full pull that collects no records publishes an empty worldlist: `pull`/`SteamSnapshot::published` (steam.rs:265-275) accept an empty `collected`, `decode_page` (862-893) accepts `{"apps": [], "have_more_results": false}`, and `load_snapshot` (372-412) loads an empty `apps` list. The module's own doc claims the opposite ("A published empty worldlist is a refusal of the pull that produced it", steam.rs:190-197) and no test covers it. A 200-with-empty-list answer (key without the IStoreService grant, gateway envelope) replaces a good snapshot at startup, after which every `steam/<appid>` lookup answers `200 []` from state.rs:364-368 — the fabricated "never heard of it" §Options' partial-snapshot rejection refused and `027-L3` does not license.
findings.fix: Fail the pull by name when a full pull yields zero records (and when a page yields zero records with have_more_results false), refuse an empty `apps` list at load as a malformed shape, and add the legs to tests/steam.rs.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/state.rs:358
findings.problem: `external_id.parse::<u64>()` accepts non-canonical spellings (`steam/007`, `steam/+7` both parse to 7, and keys.rs:60-85 admits them), while mint.rs:97 spells the appid ids from the queried spelling. So `steam/007` mints `my-game` and `steam/7` — same appid, same snapshot record — is pushed by the step-4 held check to `my-game-steam-7`, the spelling the design reserves for a different record with the same name (proposal 387-390). One game gets two load-bearing ids, the design's "appid-unique" claim (proposal 385, 399-404) is false, and one appid can consume ~120 of the 200,000 `027-B3` slots, breaking the §Risks cap arithmetic.
findings.fix: Require canonical decimal spelling before the mint path (`app.appid.to_string() == external_id`, else answer `200 []` like any non-appid token) and spell `steam-<appid>` from the snapshot record's `appid`; extend Test strategy #1 with the `007`/`+7` rows.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/store_lock.rs:116-134
findings.problem: `refuse_or_adopt` deletes a lock whose recorded pid is absent from `/proc` and takes it over (process_is_live, store_lock.rs:171-194; the module doc at 9-18 names the narrowing). §Concurrency (proposal 471-479) chose "finding it present is the named startup refusal" with runbook cleanup precisely because the fixed-tmp discipline cannot refuse a second process. A pid is not a cross-namespace identity: with a shared `<data>` volume, a `query` in another container cannot see the live `serve`'s pid, deletes the lock, and becomes the second persist-before-serve writer over the live instance's `027-L2` records.
findings.fix: Implement the designed rule (present implies refuse) and leave corpse cleanup to the Rollout 6 runbook; if stale adoption is wanted, it needs a cross-namespace-safe liveness proof (owner heartbeat rewrite or flock on the same inode) and a proposal amendment first.

findings.location: .github/workflows/check.yml:29-32
findings.problem: Rollout 3's gate work is absent from the diff: the workflow still runs `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, which now builds `apps/registry` with `rustls`/`ring` (Cargo.toml:21-26). The proposal requires this leg's scope split twice (proposal 106-109, 722-724; §Compatibility matrix 559) precisely because of `ring`'s target build script (A16). The same Rollout item's "RUSTSEC advisory screen added to the gate" (proposal 721) is also absent — the pre-existing advisories.yml is a weekly scan whose findings deliberately do not fail the job. The runner's green gate record runs neither leg.
findings.fix: Land the check.yml split (exclude bindforge-registry from the msvc leg, compile-check it on the host) plus the advisory screen, per Rollout 3.

findings.location: apps/registry/Cargo.toml:21
findings.problem: `rustls = { version = "0.23", ... }` (and `webpki-roots = "1.0"` at line 26) declares no floor, where the design names the floors as the mitigation for its largest new dependency: rustls >= 0.23.46 (RUSTSEC-2026-0346, Debug disclosing TLS secrets), rustls-webpki >= 0.103.16, webpki-roots >= 1.0.10 with the 1.x-parent note (proposal 93-101, Risks 543). Cargo.lock satisfies them today (0.23.46 / 0.103.17 / 1.0.12), but any re-resolution inside `^0.23`/`^1.0` lands on an affected version and, per the previous finding, nothing screens it.
findings.fix: Declare the floors in the manifest (`rustls = "0.23.46"`, `webpki-roots = "1.0.10"`, rustls-webpki at its floor) or enforce them via deny.toml minimum-version/advisory policy so the floor is structural rather than incidental to the lockfile.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/main.rs:338-355
findings.problem: `Config::store` resolves `partner.steam-api.com` via `to_socket_addrs` and is called at main.rs:305, before `load_or_pull_snapshot` decides whether anything will be dialed. Every hosted suite leg that runs the real binary with a key and a planted snapshot (tests/hosted_end_to_end.rs:286, 369, 389, 414, 523, 543) therefore performs a live DNS lookup for the real store authority, which Test strategy #17 forbids explicitly (proposal 693-696); the suite's greenness depends on external DNS. It also hard-fails a networkless restart whose snapshot is fresh and needed no pull.
findings.fix: Decide load-vs-pull first and resolve only on the branch that will dial; add a guard so no test resolves the authority (injectable resolver or an assertion that the resolution failure is unreachable with a fresh snapshot).

findings.location: docs/adrs/026-registry-service.md:1
findings.problem: Rollout 1's ledger annotations did not land: the diff touches only ADR-027 itself under docs/, and neither docs/adrs/026-registry-service.md nor docs/adrs/024-game-slug-identity.md mentions 027. The proposal (702-710) requires amended-by lines on `026-C1`/`026-C2`, retirement lines on `026-C6`, `026-C7`, `026-B1`-`B3`, `026-L4` amended-by, `026-L5`'s caching half, `026-R2`'s intake half, and the `024-C2` cross-reference, while this branch deletes cache.rs, upstream.rs, endpoint.rs and the 026-B1-B3 constants.
findings.fix: Land Rollout 1's annotations per 021-L4.

findings.location: docs/registry-hosting.md:1
findings.problem: The Rollout 6 operator runbook is absent. Everything proposal 736-756 names has no artifact: key custody and the CWE-526 stance, the no-URL-in-logs rule, custody of corpus/issued/retired-ids/snapshot, forcing a full refresh, deleting a crashed run's write.lock, the retired-list size check, the 026 document-pair cleanup with no migration, query as a stopped-instance tool, the restart policy bounding daily startup pulls, snapshot age as user-visible availability, cap arithmetic, and the Steam ToS obligations by name. Findings on write.lock recovery and startup pulls reference runbook steps that do not exist.
findings.fix: Write docs/registry-hosting.md with the enumerated content, per Rollout 6.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/admin.rs:231-249
findings.problem: `Answer::refused` has no 503 arm, so `AdminRefusal::Reject { status: 503 }` from state.rs:662-666 renders as `HTTP/1.1 503 Bad Request` with `{"error":"bad_request"}`; the name `retired id list full` survives only in the body prose, which is why tests/retired_ids_and_curation.rs:496-507 accepts "line or body". That contradicts the branch's own candidate-face discipline (serve.rs:304-313: the reason phrase carries the name because the status line is all the CLI shows) and the design's "named refusal" wording (proposal 440-446).
findings.fix: Add a 503 arm (reason + error token) or carry `Named` through `AdminRefusal` so the admin face renders the same names; tighten the test to assert the status line.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/persist.rs:178-203
findings.problem: `owner_only_dir` replaced an unconditional `set_permissions(0o700)` with a conditional (`if mode & 0o077 != 0`), changing a shipped invariant A2 records as "parent `0700`" for reasons of test harness behavior (the injected persist failure), not anything the proposal asked for. The owner-only ceiling is still enforced and a stricter directory now fails the write closed, so the concern is silent drift of a shipped discipline rather than a live hole.
findings.fix: Either express the intent as an explicit never-widen check separate from the shipped discipline, or inject the read-only directory in the test without changing the shipped rule; record the choice under §Deviations.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/steam.rs:58-117
findings.problem: §Budgets specifies a "new `constants.rs` family ... kept in the one file" (proposal 504-526), but the snapshot/page/retry/timeout family lives in steam.rs while constants.rs carries only the issued/retired budgets plus a pointer note. The justification at steam.rs:61-66 ("They live here until the increment that wires this resolver into the serving face ... the binary declares its own copy of `constants` and has no reader for them yet") is stale inside this diff: main.rs:39 already consumes `bindforge_registry::constants` and the resolver is wired.
findings.fix: Move the store family into constants.rs as §Budgets states and delete the stale comment.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/steam.rs:901-920
findings.problem: `normalize_store_name`/`clamp_to_name_bound` re-implement the whitespace-collapse-and-clamp rule instead of calling `discovery::game::friendly_name` "through that existing `discovery` dependency" (A7; proposal 306-312). I compared both and they are behaviorally identical, so nothing is wrong today — but a future divergence in crates/discovery/src/game.rs becomes invisible here.
findings.fix: Call `discovery::game::friendly_name` after the `char::is_control()` strip.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/steam.rs:883-887
findings.problem: A store record with a missing or non-string `name` silently becomes an empty name instead of the named malformed-envelope page refusal; A17's envelope carries `name` on every record and §The store pull names the malformed-body refusal, so this is a third unnamed posture.
findings.fix: Refuse the page with the malformed-shape name, or document that a missing name takes the empty-name posture.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/steam.rs:439-503
findings.problem: The design names the seam `StoreTransport`; the code calls it `Transport` with a `Loopback` variant, and the only production construction path is `SteamStore::for_test(address, key).with_production_transport(name)` (main.rs:354), so the name conceals which transport a hosted instance actually runs.
findings.fix: Rename to `StoreTransport` and add a `SteamStore::production(...)` constructor for the bin path.

findings.location: apps/registry/Cargo.toml:16-26 with .github/workflows/check.yml:29-32 (unchanged)
findings.problem: The C/asm native dependency (rustls' `ring` provider, plus `cc`/`find-msvc-tools`/`shlex` in Cargo.lock) landed with no CI-matrix change. The shipped `rust` job's first leg is `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` on ubuntu-latest, which now has to run ring's build script for a target with no MSVC C toolchain. The proposal prices exactly this and prescribes the fix — §Options ('the shipped whole-workspace x86_64-pc-windows-msvc compile leg (A16) drops apps/registry, which is compile-checked on the host instead'), §Risks row 1, §Compatibility matrix's Windows row ('Rollout 3 keeps apps/registry off that leg'), Rollout 3. Rollout 3's dependency half is here; its check.yml half is not in the diff. Concrete failure: the whole cargo gate goes red on the Windows leg. The runner's gate record contains no cross-target leg, so the compatibility matrix's Windows claim cannot be established from the evidence supplied.
findings.fix: Land Rollout 3's leg split beside the dependency: narrow the cross-target step to the C-free crates (or `--exclude bindforge-registry`) and add a host-target `cargo check -p bindforge-registry` step; put that leg's result in the gate record so the Windows row's coverage is evidenced.

findings.location: README.md:13-25 (unchanged) with apps/registry/Cargo.toml:21-26
findings.problem: No packaging/prerequisite story for the new C toolchain requirement: README still says the desktop-era Tauri system packages are things 'the cargo gate itself needs none of' and names only the rustup pin plus the three cargo gates. The §Compatibility matrix's Linux row states the requirement ('needs a C toolchain for ring's build script (A16, README.md prerequisite per Rollout 3)'), and A16 was recorded as verified precisely so this line would change. A contributor or an operator building the Rollout-7 binary from the README hits a build-script failure with no documented prerequisite.
findings.fix: Add the C-toolchain prerequisite line Rollout 3 names and correct the 'needs none of them' parenthetical to say which package the cargo gate now does need.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/main.rs:304-311 and :338-354 (`(steam::STORE_AUTHORITY, 443).to_socket_addrs()` before `load_or_pull_snapshot`)
findings.problem: A resolver-active startup resolves the public authority `partner.steam-api.com` before it looks at the snapshot, so every leg that configures BINDFORGE_STEAM_WEB_API_KEY without `--no-steam` (tests/common/mod.rs:503-510 deliberately withholds the `--no-steam` default there) performs an external DNS lookup: tests/data_layout.rs:131, hosted_end_to_end.rs:138, cli_end_to_end.rs:138, hosted_lookup_policy.rs:94, hosted_health_stats.rs:76, issued_entries.rs:82, mint_rule.rs:128, retired_ids_and_curation.rs:91, health_route.rs:95. findings.problem: §Concurrency adds `write.lock` because two persist-before-serve writers rename models over each other's 027-L2 records, and prescribes manual deletion as the only recovery; this code instead adopts a lock whose stamped pid is gone from /proc. No suite covers the dead-owner case: the planted-lock leg plants an empty file (treated as live) and the other covers only the honest lifecycle. PID reuse also makes a genuinely dead lock look live forever, with no runbook line for it.
findings.fix: Either keep the design's posture (a present lock is the named refusal; the Rollout-6 runbook names deleting it), or make adoption atomic and self-verifying — rename the candidate aside under `create_new` semantics, stamp, then re-read the live path and refuse if the stamp is not this run's pid — and add a suite that plants a lock carrying a provably dead pid.

findings.location: apps/registry/src/state.rs:417-423 (deepening into apps/registry/src/corpus.rs:361-365, 280-291)
findings.problem: Every mint deep-clones the whole issued Catalog (records and postings) and then Catalog::upsert runs rebuild_postings() — a full rebuild of the key→postings index — followed by a full ~30 MB re-serialization, all under the global `mutations` mutex that serializes mints and admin mutations for up to 64 request threads. The design's §Concurrency names this exact thing as forbidden: "a mint inserts the new key's posting rather than rebuilding the index". At 027-B3's 200k-record cap each novel-key mint pays the whole-model O(n) clone + O(n) index rebuild + O(n) serialize three times over, making the cloned postings copy pure waste; 027-S1 makes first-time steam keys the day-one ordinary path. Scale evidence: the suite's own 200k startup-load leg (one O(n) parse + postings build) takes 4.09s in debug (test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 4.09s), so a per-mint hold of the one mutex near the cap is multi-hundred-ms-to-seconds. The design's §Risks write-amplification row prices only the whole-document rewrite and names the posting-insert as the in-memory mitigation; the clone+rebuild delta is unpriced, and the Rollout-4 deliverable ("issued-document rewrite measured at 100k and 200k records, recorded in §Budgets") has no artifact in the reviewable diff.
findings.fix: Give Catalog a mint seam that inserts the record and pushes the new key's single posting into the existing postings in game_id order (one mint adds exactly one posting) instead of calling rebuild_postings, and avoid the deep postings clone (mutate the clone's postings in place, or swap the model through a single-slot Arc swap). No mint may rebuild the index. Then land the Rollout-4 measurement of the issued rewrite at 100k and 200k records beside the §Budgets figure.

findings.location: §Budgets / §Risks — "`MAX_STEAM_PAGE_OCTETS = 12_582_912` — the response *read* budget for one page … not a worst case, since over-bound store names make a page's true size unbounded and the over-cap page is the residual §Risks carries"

Over-bound names are not the only way a *legal* page breaches 12 MiB: the body carries JSON string escapes, so a name at its 128-octet decoded bound serializes at up to 2x when quote- or backslash-heavy (~340 octets per record, ~17 MiB for the pinned 50k page) and more for characters the encoder emits as `\u00XX`. §Risks also states the cost as only "a page refusal that keeps the previous snapshot until `027-B2`'s age bound" — the steady-state half; on a cold instance with no snapshot the same named page refusal is the named startup refusal, and the operator's only way to bind is `--no-steam`, i.e. every Steam key answering `503` and every bound CLI scan failing closed (§Compatibility matrix).
